desk.headline: HEPS up 42% to €4.27 (from €3.01) on strong jewellery demand; no numeric outlook
results: Headline earnings per share rose 42% to €4.27 from €3.01; diluted HEPS rose to €4.26 from €3.00.
Headline earnings climbed to €2.51bn from €1.77bn a year earlier.
The company described sustained double-digit sales growth, led by its jewellery houses.
No interim dividend was declared; Richemont pays one dividend a year.

guidance.summary: Richemont gives no numbers for the rest of the year. It expects conditions to stay volatile, plans to keep costs tight while investing in its brands, and says the watch recovery may be uneven.

points: Demand for the brands' signature jewellery and watch lines stayed strong across most regions.
Raw-material costs remain high, and price increases were kept measured, with one price policy worldwide.
Watch demand in China is still soft; management expects China to recover over time.
Japan's growth came mainly from local shoppers rather than tourists.
The watch division is working towards a high single-digit margin for the full year.
call.source: Results presentation coverage: Investing.com, 13 Nov 2026; Poland Insight, 13 Nov 2026; ad-hoc-news, Nov 2026

watch: Whether jewellery growth holds up after slowing in the second quarter.
Watchmaker margins and any recovery in Chinese demand.
Gold and other raw-material costs, and US tariff effects, on gross margin.
